item.title: Author Post
item.content:encoded:
I assume that after a while, that includes repeating the 'failure to keep one of them out'?

No, that was a fluke caused by one of the participants breaking character after two years of success. After 7 comes in, though, when one role gets over-tedious they can swap and take breaks. So my thought was it needn't necessarily happen again. Little flukes and hiccups might happen from time to time, but they're not common.

Spoiler...
...reliopS

SCP-1780 details another such fluke in one of the incident logs.

And what WOULD happen if they stop turning them away?

Well, in addition to Dr. Xyank completely disappearing from the rest of causality for at least several thousand iterations rather than just 7, eventually there would be so many Xyanks in the room that every subsequent one would open the door, see a wall of writing, angry, crushed and wailing Xyanks, on the other side, and be unable to enter the anomaly in the first place.

I realize this has a lot of implications about time and time travel being at least a little logically inconsistent in the Foundationverse, but that's rather the point. I like to take the angle that "there is no canon, everything is canon" regarding the wiki and its content. And that practically requires an inconsistent causality.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Here there be spoilers...
You have been warned.

1. Dr. Xyank et. al. reproduce the 084 phenomenon under laboratory conditions. However, the math was fudged up and the radius of effect was much larger than anticipated.
2. When he left to check his notes, he found himself in an isolated pocket of time back in his office. Periodically, another copy of himself enters the room.
3. By Iteration 6, all copies have come to a consensus of what has gone on, and developed a strategy to keep all future copies from entering.
4a. Dr. Xyank is successfully intercepted by his copies and turned back to terminate the experiment. He later learns more about time travel, such that a future version of himself can drop off an important package for him.
4b. From within the anomaly, the cycle continues infinitely. After 42,872 iterations, one of the copies snaps and spills the beans, breaking symmetry. Rather than attempt to escape and risk damaging the timeline, the non-symmetrical copy decides to contain himself with the other 6 already trapped by the anomaly.

This is horrible, because although it appears to all of us that the paradox has been resolved, it has not be resolved from those trapped within the paradox. The ritual of opening the door and turning the next iteration away must be performed in exactly the same manner every cycle. For eternity.

Honestly… I may have been a little too ambitious with the time-fuckery I was attempting here…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Nah, it wasn't.

I added that to increase the alienation of the secondary timeline. It's meant to be a little jarring and disorienting, because the anomaly is "over" from the point of view of bulk causality, and yet it's still running infinitely from within.

It's really bloody hard to map a perpendicular timeline and still make it comprehensible. This was the best compromise I could come up with.
